1.2.3.7-r1.burton_quote: cause this malady by themselves, especially if their bodies be otherwise disposed to Melancholy

1.2.3.7-r2.burton_quote: Envy so gnaws many men’s hearts, that they become altogether melancholy

1.2.3.7-r3.burton_quote: As a moth gnaws a garment, so, saith Chrysostom, doth envy consume a man

1.2.3.7-r4.burton_quote: I have read, saith Marcus Aurelius, Greek, Hebrew, Chaldee Authors, I have consulted with many wise men, for a remedy for envy, I could find none, but to renounce all happiness, and to be a wretch, and miserable forever

1.2.3.7-r5.burton_quote: Every other sin hath some pleasure annexed to it, or will admit of an excuse; envy alone wants both. Other sins last but for a while, the gut may be satisfied, anger remits, hatred hath an end, envy never ceaseth

1.2.3.7-r6.burton_quote: that a private man should be so much glorified
1.2.3.7-r6.translation: (that a private man's name should be) raised above the prince's

1.2.3.7-r7.burton_quote: because she had a better horse, and better furniture, as if she had hurt them with it; they were much offended

1.2.3.7-r8.burton_quote: Myrsine an Attic wench, was murdered of her fellows, because she did excel the rest in beauty
